sentences.text: The petition was filed before the LAC and referred to by the Collector for determination of the court.

2. The brief factual matrix leading to the present petition is that the Government vide notification bearing No. F.11(19)/2001/L&B/LA/20112 dt. 21.03.2003 issued by the Lt. Governor of Delhi under Section 4 of the Act, Government intended to acquire about 2480 Bigha 01 Biswas of land with its specification mentioned in the notification for public purpose namely 'Rohini Residential Scheme'
under the "Planned Development of Delhi".
LAC no. 142/ 2016 (Award No. 16/200506/DC(NW)) Jeet Ram V. Union of India Page no. 2 of 12 3.

sentences.text: The Government vide consequent Declaration/notification No. F.11 (19)/2001/L&B/LA/28176 dated 19.03.2004 issued pursuant thereto under Section 6 of the Act, acquired 2480 Bigha 01 Biswas land (as detailed in the statement under Section 19 of the Act), situated in the revenue estate of village Mubarakpur Dabas, Delhi.
The LAC (N/W)

after completing all the requisite formalities as provided under the Act, announced the Award bearing no. 16 of 200506 dated 14.09.2005 u/s 11 of the Act in respect of 2480 bighas 01 biswas out of the aforesaid said land and awarded a compensation at the uniform rate of Rs.15,70,000/ per acre (or Rs. 3,27,083.33/ per bigha) for the entire said land in addition to other statutory benefits and interests.

4. It is stated that the petitioners are the recorded owner/bhumidhar of the land comprised in Khasra no. 2/23 (309), 4/3/1 (402), 19/19 (416) i.e. total area measuring 12 Bigha and 07 Biswas, having share as per the revenue record, situated in the revenue estate of Village Mubarakpur Dabas, Delhi (in short, the said land).
5. It is stated that the petitioners are entitled to receive the compensation amount of the actual prevailing market value of the said land.

The actual physical possession of the said land is with the petitioners as the physical possession of the land has not been taken and the respondents shall take possession thereof from the petitioners.

The ld. LAC passed the award in a mechanical way without applying the mind and without going through LAC no. 142/ 2016 (Award No. 16/2005 06/DC(NW)) Jeet Ram V. Union of India Page no. 3 of 12 the claim filed by the petitioners, as such the award is not acceptable to the petitioner, and they has received the awarded amount under protest and without prejudice to their rights.

sentences.text: The LAC failed to take note of the actual and practical market value of the said land and had adopted a narrow approach while observing that no proof of claim market value is attached.
The LAC has not assessed the actual market value of the said land in spite having knowledge of the fair market value adjudicated by the courts.
The LAC has failed to properly appreciate the quality, status, potentiality and development of the said land and its surroundings.

6. As such the ld. LAC has failed to take note of the judicial pronouncements and the government policy of 10% yearly escalation in the market value of the said land.

9. It is stated that the respondent no.2 has allotted the adjoining Rohini residential land to persons for residential as well as commercial purposes for more than Rs. 6000/ per square yards and that too, only to those who has applied for the plots/flats and shops well in advance, which fact shows that that the land for residential and commercial purposes was not easily LAC no. 142/ 2016 (Award No. 16/200506/DC(NW)) Jeet Ram V. sentences.text: The respondent no.2 has been allotting the plots at the remotest and undeveloped the land, therefore, it is clear that the respondent no.2 cannot gain/earn profit at the cost of causing loss to the petitioner.
10. The ld. LAC, while passing the award has erred in not taking into account the devaluation of the money.
The ld. LAC should have taken note of the loss and injury suffered by the petitioner.

The ld.
LAC has grossly erred in directing the deduction of tax, from the amount of compensation of the said land as no tax from the amount of compensation and interest thereupon could be deducted.
It is stated that the petitioner has claimed the compensation for the acquire land @ Rs.2000/ per square yards in addition to Rs. 25,000/ per bigha, solatium amount along with interest.
They claimed interest on the solatium amount and any other relief to which petitioner is entitled.
11. Written statement has been filed on behalf of respondent no.1/Union of India and, it is, inter alia,
submitted that the petition is not maintainable as the petitioner has been filed on false and fictitious grounds.
The ld. LAC has already assessed the market value of the said land, taking into consideration the prevailing market rates at the time of the passing of the notification under Section 4 of the Act.
The said land was acquired at the instance of DDA, therefore DDA is a necessary party.

LAC.
The area of the land and other amenities/facilities were also taken into consideration while assessing the compensation.

13. It is submitted that the compensation awarded by ld. LAC is adequate, sufficient just and legal and is based on cogent and reliable evidence, therefore, there is no scope for enhancement of the compensation amount.
The present reference petition is also barred by limitation.
The copy of the reference petition has not been forwarded to DDA, though the DDA is a beneficiary party, therefore,
DDA is not liable to pay any interest on the delayed period.

It is submitted that as per the directions of Land and Building Department, after announcement of the Award reference should be forwarded by LAC within 60 days from the date of filing of the reference.
The present petition has not been forwarded to the court within 60 days therefore, DDA/beneficiary of land is not liable to pay interest thereupon.

14. It is submitted that the said land, after acquisition the possession of the said land bearing Khasra No. 2//23 (309), 4//3/1 (402) has been taken over by DDA but the possession of the land bearing Khasra No. 19//19 (4 16) has not been handed over to DDA.

It is submitted that the compensation passed by ld. LAC is legal, adequate, just and fair and the same has been awarded by ld. LAC after taking into consideration all the factors relevant for determining the compensation, as such the petitioner is not entitled for grant of enhancement of compensation.

All the other averments made by the petitioner in the reference petition are denied in toto and it is prayed that the prayer of the petitioner is false,
frivolous and vexatious and without any cause of action, therefore, the reference petition filed by the petitioner is liable to be dismissed with cost.
15.

22. Since the fair market value of the land situated in village Mubarakpur Dabas and covered by the award in question has already been determined by this court, this court has no reason or evidence to deviate therefrom.

In view of the aforesaid discussion, this court also determines the same enhanced market value as awarded in the case of Savitri Devi (supra) in the present case, in so far as the acquisition of the land of petitioners is concerned.

23. In the case of Savitri Devi (supra), this court had adjudicated the market value of land of village Mubarkpur Dabas acquired through Award No. 16 of 200506 dated 14.09.2005 as Rs. 19,45,800/
per acre i.e. an enhancement of Rs. 3,75,800/ per acre has been given.
There is no evidence on record to gather that the land of the petitioners herein was in any way inferior to the land involved in Savitri Devi (supra).
The petitioners are, accordingly entitled to the same compensation for their land as was awarded in Savitri Devi (supra).
This court adjudicate the market value of land of the petitioners as Rs.19,45,800/ per acre thereby giving an enhancement of Rs.3,75,800/ per acre.
